quest.title: Cold Case Commission
quest.description: You arrive at the Adventurers' Guild in Sumeru. Katheryne seems to have a very tricky commission for your docket...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x875, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

talks.objective: Go to the Sumeru Adventurers' Guild and talk to Katheryne

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Ah, perfect! It's you two. I have a commission here that has your names written all over it. In fact, I'd even go so far as to say you're the only ones for the job.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The only ones for the job? Huh, if our help is really that important, it's probably some Archon-class commission, right?

choices.text: I've never heard of that classification before.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Hehe... The Adventurers' Guild doesn't employ that kind of classification system. In fact, this commission is also probably not nearly as intimidating as what you're expecting.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: All it asks us to do is to find a missing person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Then why did you say we were the only ones for the job?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: I came across this commission while reviewing our backlog not too long ago.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: It seems simple, but our records indicate that over a dozen successive efforts to complete it have all ended in failure, despite attempts by several accomplished and renowned adventurers.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: With the reputation of the Adventurers' Guild and the performance of the Sumeru branch at stake, it's in our best interest to assign this commission to the adventurer with the highest completion rate over the past few years...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Well, that's us for sure!

choices.text: Flattery will get you everywhere with Paimon.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Hehe... All I'm asking is for you to give it your best shot.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: If it proves to be beyond your capabilities as well, I'll talk to the commissioner about canceling the commission.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, so who are we looking for, and what is it about this commission that's made it so hard to complete?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: This commission was jointly issued by the residents of Vimara Village. They say one of their own villagers has gone missing...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: But the problem is... They don't know the missing person's name. They can only provide information about his general appearance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... They're all from the same village, but they don't even know his name?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, if so many adventurers have failed to complete this commission, maybe this "missing villager" doesn't exist at all? Could it be some sort of... prank or something?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Unlikely. Several villagers came by to issue the commission, and judging by their appearance and tone of voice, they seemed incredibly sincere. It certainly didn't seem like a joke to them.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Besides, putting up a commission requires a processing fee. There aren't many upsides to a prank that costs Mora to carry out.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: True, that would be a little strange...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: In any case, it would probably be best to go to Vimara Village and ask around first. The Adventurers' Guild does have some information on hand, but I would say anything you can learn directly from the villagers would be far more reliable. The best way to avoid misdirection is to go to the source.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, then let's go! Paimon is starting to get really curious about this whole thing!

choices.text: But, I can't guarantee we'll be able to complete it, either.
But sure, we're happy to take this on. Which Archon do you need us to deal with today?

dialogues.speaker: Bahram
dialogues.text: I really hope he's okay. Please, we're counting on you to find him.

dialogues.speaker: Bahram
dialogues.text: Hello there! You looking to buy something? I do business in this area...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, no, no. We're adventurers! Katheryne sent us to look into a commission here in Vimara Village...

dialogues.speaker: Bahram
dialogues.text: Ah, so you're here about that, then... *sigh* You're not the first, that's for sure. We've certainly made a lot of trouble for you all.

dialogues.speaker: Bahram
dialogues.text: To be honest, we aren't holding out much hope. Many adventurers have made their way out here, confident they'd be able to help us, only to leave soon after with nothing to show for their efforts.

dialogues.speaker: Bahram
dialogues.text: We've pretty much had it up to here in questions, and the area around the village has practically been overturned in search of clues. But, no one has been able to make any headway...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this person we're looking for... What's his name? Where did he live? Does he have any relatives?

dialogues.speaker: Bahram
dialogues.text: I don't know. I really have no clue. I couldn't tell you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okaayy... Guess you really are sick of answering questions.

dialogues.speaker: Bahram
dialogues.text: Ah... I'm sorry. I didn't mean to sound short with you. I was actually just giving you my answer to your questions.

choices.text: So those three questions are a no go, then...

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: I know it may seem like we don't have anything to offer by way of information, but I promise you we all have a very strong impression of him. When you live in the same village as someone, you develop a lot of memories together, y'know?

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: We just don't know the specifics. Maybe we did at one point, but that information is long gone by now...

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: At least, that's what everyone in the village seems to think. We've all exchanged what we know, and that was the only logical conclusion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, specifics aside, then... What kind of person was he?

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: Young guy, in his early twenties probably. Incredibly kind sort of person, always willing to lend a helping hand...

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: I'd chat with him when I didn't have any customers. I even saw him stick out his neck for others on more than one occasion, haha... Very interesting guy, that one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that you've started talking about him, you don't seem nearly as down in the dumps as you did before. Seems like he left a pretty good impression on you.

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: But of course! Everyone in the village is pretty fond of him. We wouldn't have issued that commission otherwise.

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: There aren't many young people like him nowadays, so genuine and pure. To think that he just up and disappeared one day... I just hope nothing bad happened...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could he have just... moved away without telling anyone?

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: No. He's not the type to leave without saying goodbye. And anyway, moving away without being seen by a single person in the village? There's no way he would've been able to manage that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... All right. Thanks for the information! We're gonna go ask around some more.

choices.text: Is there anything else you can tell us?

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Is that guests I hear?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi, Grandpa Amadhiah! We're here to help you look for the guy that's gone missing.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's what brings you to these parts! Coming all this way for our sake... That's so very kind of you. With your help, I trust that young man's case is in good hands.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could you tell us a bit about him?

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Of course! I'm happy to help any way I can.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: With my failing eyesight, I'm afraid I can't offer much about his appearance. But, I do remember hearing the sound of his voice... Not recently, of course. That loss has left me feeling quite empty.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: I don't think his parents are still living in the village. But, somehow, he never seemed lonely. In fact, he was usually the one offering companionship to others.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: He would often take time to visit the elderly or play with the orphans in the village.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: And whenever someone had something on their mind, he was there to listen with open ears. He always knew just what to say.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: As the village chief, I owe him many thanks. Helping villagers navigate difficult moments in their lives should have been one of my responsibilities, but he was often the one rising to the occasion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, he seems like such a nice and gentle person! No wonder his disappearance affected you all so much.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, um... You wouldn't happen to know any details about his name, address, or family situation, right?

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: *sigh*... I'm ashamed to admit it, but... I just can't remember. No matter how you look at it, I should know those things, but for some reason, no matter how hard I try to remember, the information just doesn't come. Perhaps my age really has caught up with me this time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... It's okay! There's no need to force yourself to try and remember. We'll figure something out...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}? What do you think?

choices.text: There's probably more to this case than meets the eye.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks so too! Like the name thing... It's so weird that no one remembers his name.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And nobody has been able to tell us anything about his family or where he lived... It's like this guy's been erased from reality or something.

choices.text: I would say it's more like...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... So you're saying, it's not that he's been "erased" necessarily, but more like he never "existed" to begin with?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, Paimon's gonna need some time to process that one... Someone who only exists in people's memories...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Could it be like what happened with Greater Lord Rukkhadevata? Like some sort of mass alteration of people's memories...?)
You two are the adventurers who just arrived, right? You're here for the Vimara Village commission?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, sure are! We were just looking into the case...
I'm so glad to hear that! Thank goodness you haven't given up. I've been so worried the Adventurers' Guild might cancel our commission...

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: My name is Atossa, by the way. I grew up here in Vimara Village. Anyway, I just wanted to say... Please keep searching for our missing villager. I'm begging you. You have to find him...

choices.text: I'm sure we'll track him down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! No need to worry! We'll give it our best shot! So, were you close to the missing villager? Are there any leads you can give us?

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: Hmm... I'm not sure this counts as a lead, but follow me. There's a place I'd like to show you.

choices.text: We'll certainly try our best.
He's someone who only exists in people's memories.
A lot of things are not adding up.

talks.objective: Go to the place indicated by Atossa

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this the place? Under this tree?

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: Yep. I know it doesn't look like much, but this place is very meaningful to me. It's so full of memories...

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: We used to always sit together under this tree and talk. Sometimes, we would look up at the clouds in the sky, or stop to feel the wind against our skin. We could sit there for hours at a time, never realizing how long it had been...

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: I was actually adopted by the people of Vimara Village. The Forest Rangers found me in the woods as a child.

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: I was surrounded by such good people, and growing up in the village was so lively. Still... there were times when I couldn't help but feel incredibly alone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alone?

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: *sigh*... How should I put it? When something's bothering you, or when you have good news to share, you always want to talk about it with somebody. But, for the longest time, I didn't know who I could talk to, or if I should say anything at all...

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: Everyone has their own problems to deal with. Even if I might want to confide in others, I don't want to become a burden.

choices.text: I think I get what you mean.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: Really? You know exactly how I feel?

choices.text: I used to have someone like that, a family member that I could talk to no matter what.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aww!

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: Wow, that sounds really nice. You're quite lucky. When it comes to our missing villager, well... I guess you could say that, to me, he felt like both — a family member I could rely on, and a friend who could really understand me.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: No matter what came my way, I knew I could always talk to him...

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: He was so thoughtful and pure... and patient, too. Whenever I talked to him, he would always seem so interested, as if the things I was describing were just as important to him as they were to me.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: ...Ever since he disappeared, there's been so much I wanted to tell him...

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: No, no, none of those things matters now. I just really want to see him again...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, you two must have been really close...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did he ever tell you anything about himself?

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: Hmm... He mostly just talked about interesting things he saw around the village... He'd share a lot of his own wild ideas as well...

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: Oh right, I did ask him about his parents once... But, all he said was, "They're not here anymore."

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: I didn't know whether that meant they had left the village or passed away, and I didn't want to pry...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, still not much to go off of...

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: Ah, look at me, talking your ear off and still nothing to show for it. I'm sorry I wasn't more help...

choices.text: Don't say that.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: The last time I talked this much in one go was when we were still together.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: Come to think of it, every time we talked, it always seemed to be around dusk, just like right now.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: Time always passed by really slowly. Even when it felt like we'd been talking for hours, the sun would still be at the same position in the sky...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, time always seems to pass slower when you're relaxed, right? ...Huh? What's wrong, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: It was always the same time of day...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Based on what we've learned, this is definitely not a regular missing person's case...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (What Atossa just told us about time could be the key to unraveling this whole mystery...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Hey, look at those Hilichurls over there... Doesn't it seem like they're acting a little strange?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, the Abyss Order. Could they be the ones behind all of this?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-oh, we've been spotted. Quick, get ready to fight!

choices.text: And time never seemed to pass...
You helped us understand him better.
But now, I have a lot of friends who understand me, and would be happy to hear me out.
That's what family is for.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: While you two are out searching, I'll also try and see what I can remember... If I think of something, I'll be sure to let you know.

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: Thank you so much! I wasn't expecting monsters to show up. If you hadn't been here, I'm not sure what I would've done...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It was no trouble!

choices.text: The question we should be asking now is...

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: Hmm, now that I think about it, the Hilichurls around Vimara Village have been a lot more active lately...

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: They seem agitated, and would often attack anything in sight. Chief Amadhiah doesn't allow the children to play in the area around the village anymore.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Maybe the Abyss Order really is involved...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, we should head back and check out the situation in Vimara Village just in case. If the Abyss Order is plotting something, that could spell trouble for the villagers.

choices.text: What is the Abyss Order doing around here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We made it to Vimara Village! Why don't we talk to some of the villagers to learn a bit more about the missing guy?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If this commission is really as challenging as Katheryne made it out to be, we're gonna need to carry out a very detailed investigation!
